# Body drawing margin clearance

Original OOXML/PNG controls generated by tools/anchor_page_clearance_fixture.py.
Fifteen sections cross absent/12pt/48pt headers with margin- and paragraph-relative
negative offsets, a page-relative negative offset, and an oversized 900pt image.
The 30pt top margin and 20pt header distance isolate effective writing boundaries
of 30, 32 and 68pt. The reference application supplies the PDF/PNGs; the recorder stores
source/PDF SHA-256 hashes and image bounds. All fifteen native pages were inspected.

The reference application places a margin-relative +100pt image at 130/132/168pt: the position uses
header clearance rather than merely the stored 30pt margin. Paragraph-relative
-90pt images begin at -60/-58/-22pt. Completely off-page small images have no PDF
image object, while oversized images at the same origins remain visible. A
page-relative -10pt offset stays -10pt regardless of header height. Therefore a
general page-top clamp would contradict the reference application and is not applied.

Relevant clauses: ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 17.6.11 (pgMar), 20.4.2.11 (positionV),
and 20.4.3.5 (ST_RelFromV). The margin reference follows the body edge resulting
from the header-clearance rule. This records the reference application's interpretation; the vertical
reference enumeration alone does not specify the interaction.

Unit checks compare native frames and retain editing, package preservation,
export/reopen and undo. Browser masks compare all visible drawing ink in both
directions within one pixel before/after editing and reopening. Negative origins,
off-page drawings and oversized drawings are retained, with painting clipped by
the page. Native PDF bounds do not measure antialiasing or glyph fidelity.
